title: Speech writing
examples: How do I make my speech sound more exciting?
What is the difference between talking to a crowd and writing a speech?
Should I use slang in my formal speech?

explain.say: Today we are learning how to write a powerful speech.
First, use direct address to speak right to your audience.
Next, use rhetoric to make your words persuasive and memorable.
The ending must summarize your main ideas and suggest a clear next step.

items: Final Sentence: Tell them what to do

explain.say: For an everyday example, think about a school fundraiser speech.

items: Mention how much money is needed.
End by asking everyone to donate today.

explain.say: A common mistake is sounding too academic or formal always.

faq.q: How do I start my speech so people listen?
faq.a: You can start with a surprising statistic or a short, relevant story. You could also ask a question to make them think right away.
asks: What is a good opening line?
How do I grab attention at the start?

faq.q: What exactly is rhetoric in speech writing?
faq.a: Rhetoric is the art of persuasion, using language carefully to convince your audience. It helps you choose the right words for the right moment.
asks: How do I sound more persuasive?

faq.q: Should I use slang when I am giving a formal speech?
faq.a: It depends on your audience; if you know them well, some slang is fine. Otherwise, stick to clear, standard language to sound professional.
asks: How formal should my tone be?

faq.a: Your conclusion needs to wrap everything up neatly and tell the audience what action to take next. Do not introduce new ideas here.
asks: How do I finish my speech strongly?
What is the purpose of the ending?

faq.q: Is it better to write everything out or use notes?
faq.a: It is best to write a detailed outline, but practice speaking from key points rather than reading every word. This keeps you sounding natural.
asks: Should I memorize my speech word for word?
How much should I write down?

facts: A direct address involves speaking directly to the people listening.
Rhetoric includes techniques like repetition to emphasize points.
A strong conclusion often includes a clear call to action.
Varying your tone keeps the audience engaged throughout the speech.

quiz.say: Which technique is best for making your main points feel very important?
quiz.why: Repeating a word or phrase at the beginning of successive clauses adds rhythmic emphasis.

wrong.1: This is good for engagement, but repetition is better for building weight.
wrong.2: This can confuse the audience, even if the words are impressive.
wrong.3: Facts alone are informative but lack the emotional punch of repetition.

quiz.say: If you want your audience to volunteer for a clean-up day, what should your ending focus on?
quiz.why: The ending must tell the audience exactly what you want them to do next.

wrong.0: This is polite, but it leaves the audience unsure of what to do next.
wrong.1: Summarizing is good, but it must be followed by a clear next step.
wrong.2: A story is a good opener, but it distracts from the main point in the conclusion.

quiz.say: When speaking to a group of students about recycling, what is the most effective way to address them?
quiz.why: Using 'you' makes the speech feel personal and directly relevant to the listener.

wrong.0: This creates distance and sounds like a lecture from a high place.
wrong.1: The third person removes the connection between the speaker and the audience.
wrong.3: This makes it sound like the speaker is speaking only for the group.
